source_text.body:
Use specs to guide Copilot through backend endpoint work
A developer used Copilot to execute backend work (new endpoint, auth logic update, webhook handling, tests) once a clear spec defined the scope.
Done with
GH
GitHub Copilot
What they did
On a small SaaS backend task, the developer first wrote a one-screen spec listing the goal, non-goals, allowed files, constraints, and acceptance checks. With that scope set, they used Copilot for the implementation work and repetitive edits across things like a new endpoint, auth changes, webhook handling, and tests, while other chat models helped draft the spec and think through edge cases.
How it went
They say this reduced drift versus letting Copilot run from a vague TODO and helped keep fast code generation aligned to existing patterns. The stated limitation is that Copilot still improvises if the task is under-specified, especially on larger changes.
Worth knowing
Their rule of thumb was not to delegate until they could write acceptance checks; for bigger changes, they sometimes added a planning layer to break the checklist into file-level tasks.
Try it yourself
with
GitHub Copilot
Copy prompt
Here is my spec: [paste spec covering new endpoint, auth change, webhook handling and tests]. Implement it in my repo, staying strictly within the scope of the spec. Add tests for each part and run them. You're done when the tests pass, and give me a summary of every file you changed.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/GithubCopilot/comments/1rbnb3a/copilot_is_amazing_at_typing_its_bad_at_reading
